chunks: With every individual there are two angels who protect him; when destiny approaches they let it have its own way with him. Certainly, the appointed time is a protective shield (against the events which occur before it).
ai.seo_question: What is the role of angels in relation to human destiny and appointed time in Shia theology?
ai.summary: Imam Ali (peace be upon him) elucidates the dual mechanism of divine protection and predestination, noting that two angels guard each individual until their appointed time (ajal) arrives, at which point they release their hold. This concept underscores the Shia understanding of 'ajal' as a fortified shield, ensuring that no event overtakes a person before their divinely decreed term, blending the reality of angelic guardianship with the inevitability of fate.
